test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 04 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 4.
solution:
The correct answer is '**has been**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage refers to an ongoing and persistent issue over the years, making "has been" the appropriate choice to indicate the continuous nature of the problem.
 
• "Has been" suggests that this issue has existed over time and continues to be relevant.
 
• Other options ("will be", "have been", "is") do not fit as well in conveying the prolonged and continuing nature of the problem in the Indian job market.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

Complete Passage: *Students want (1)* *employability__* * as the primary outcome of higher education. Hence, practical experience becomes (2)________ valuable to a student’s degree. Indian students are highly (3)________ at theoretical learning but lack practical training. This (4) __has been__ an issue for decades in the Indian job market. In order to address this (5)________ issue, state governments have to take a lead. The AP government in the past three years have made efforts to bridge this long-lasting gap between theoretical and practical learning of the students.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• "Has been" indicates an ongoing issue, which is fitting in the context of this passage that discusses a long-standing problem in the job market.
 
• "Will be" is future tense, which does not match the passage's indication that the issue has been existing for decades.
 
• "Have been" would not be appropriate here because the subject ("This") is singular, and "has been" is the correct verb form.
 
• "Is" is present tense, but the passage emphasizes that the issue has existed for a long time, which makes the past perfect form ("has been") the best choice.
